definitions.definition: The study of God using the tools and ideas of physics.
definitions.example: Like using math to understand how God might create the universe.

definitions.definition: The basic, underlying reality from which everything else comes.
definitions.example: Like the ground that supports a building, but you can't see the ground by looking at the building.

definitions.definition: A previous research paper that described the Son and Holy Spirit using physics ideas.
definitions.example: Like a chapter in a book that sets up the main characters.

definitions.definition: A Greek word meaning 'Word' or 'reason,' used in the Bible to describe Jesus as the logical structure of the universe.
definitions.example: Like the blueprint that makes a building stand up straight.

definitions.definition: A pattern or rule that stays the same even when things change around it.
definitions.example: Like the fact that 2+2 always equals 4, no matter what you're counting.

definitions.definition: Rules in physics that say certain things (like energy) can't be created or destroyed, only changed form.
definitions.example: Like how the total amount of money in a closed jar stays the same even if you move coins around.

definitions.definition: The idea that all the information in a volume of space can be encoded on its boundary, like a 3D image stored on a 2D surface.
definitions.example: Like a credit card hologram that shows a 3D picture even though it's flat.

definitions.definition: The process of making something real or turning potential into reality.
definitions.example: Like turning a recipe into an actual cake.

definitions.definition: A rule in quantum mechanics that tells you the probability of finding a particle in a certain place.
definitions.example: Like a weather forecast that says there's a 70% chance of rain.

definitions.definition: A mathematical group used to describe the strong nuclear force that holds quarks together.
definitions.example: Like a special kind of symmetry that governs how particles interact.

definitions.definition: The force that holds the center of an atom together, keeping protons and neutrons from flying apart.
definitions.example: Like super-strong glue that sticks the tiniest particles together.

definitions.definition: Tiny particles that are the building blocks of protons and neutrons.
definitions.example: Like LEGO bricks that make up bigger things like atoms.

definitions.definition: The property that quarks can never be found alone; they are always stuck together inside larger particles.
definitions.example: Like a magnet that always has a north and south pole—you can't have just one.

definitions.definition: A field that carries the strong nuclear force between quarks, like a force field that glues them together.
definitions.example: Like an invisible rubber band that gets stronger the more you stretch it.

definitions.definition: The smallest amount of energy that empty space can have, even when all particles are removed.
definitions.example: Like the lowest hum a guitar string can make, even when you're not plucking it.

definitions.definition: The lowest possible energy level of a system, like the 'resting' state.
definitions.example: Like a ball sitting at the bottom of a hill—it can't go any lower.

definitions.definition: The state of empty space in quantum physics, which is not truly empty but full of tiny, temporary particles and energy.
definitions.example: Like a seemingly empty room that's actually full of invisible dust motes and air currents.

definitions.definition: Particles that pop in and out of existence in empty space, too quickly to be directly observed.
definitions.example: Like bubbles that appear and disappear in a fizzy drink.

definitions.definition: A disturbance or ripple in a field that creates a particle or wave.
definitions.example: Like a bump in a rug that makes a visible lump.

definitions.definition: Present everywhere at the same time.
definitions.example: Like the air around you—it's everywhere, even if you can't see it.

definitions.definition: A force that pushes two metal plates together when they are very close in empty space, caused by the vacuum energy between them.
definitions.example: Like two boats being pushed together by waves in the water between them.

definitions.definition: A tiny change in the energy levels of a hydrogen atom caused by vacuum fluctuations.
definitions.example: Like a very small adjustment to the pitch of a musical note.

definitions.definition: Temporary changes in the energy of empty space, where particles and antiparticles appear and disappear.
definitions.example: Like tiny ripples on the surface of a still pond.

definitions.definition: The surface that stores the information for a hologram, like a photographic plate that creates a 3D image.
definitions.example: Like the film in a camera that captures the picture.

definitions.definition: The 3D image or reality that comes from a holographic plate or source.
definitions.example: Like the movie you see on a screen, which comes from the film in the projector.

definitions.definition: The mathematical description of empty space in quantum field theory, which has a minimum energy.
definitions.example: Like the 'off' setting on a machine that still uses a tiny bit of power.

definitions.definition: A theory that combines quantum mechanics and special relativity to describe how particles and fields interact.
definitions.example: Like a rulebook for how tiny particles behave and create forces.

definitions.definition: A specific way a system can vibrate or oscillate, like a particular frequency of a wave.
definitions.example: Like different notes on a guitar string—each note is a different mode of vibration.

definitions.definition: The study of heat, energy, and how they move and change form.
definitions.example: Like the science of how a refrigerator keeps food cold or how an engine runs.
definitions.first_appearance: V The Father and the Floor

definitions.definition: A theorem that says every symmetry in nature leads to a conservation law (like energy conservation).
definitions.example: Like how if a system looks the same no matter when you look at it, energy is conserved.

definitions.definition: A fundamental symmetry of nature that says the laws of physics stay the same if you flip charge, parity (mirror image), and time all at once.
definitions.example: Like a video that looks the same if you reverse it, mirror it, and swap colors—all at the same time.

definitions.definition: The study of salvation—how people are saved from sin and its consequences.
definitions.example: Like learning about how a lifeguard rescues a drowning person.
definitions.first_appearance: Not explicitly in text, but related to grace floor concept

definitions.definition: The study of sin—what it is and how it affects people.
definitions.example: Like studying the rules of a game and what happens when you break them.
definitions.first_appearance: Not explicitly in text, but related to entropy and decoherence

definitions.definition: The process of becoming more holy or set apart for God.
definitions.example: Like cleaning and polishing a dirty coin until it shines.

definitions.definition: The act of making up for a wrong or restoring a broken relationship, especially between humans and God.
definitions.example: Like saying sorry and fixing a broken toy to make things right with a friend.

definitions.definition: A mapping between two structures that shows they are essentially the same in form or function.
definitions.example: Like a map of a subway system that has the same connections as the real tracks.

definitions.definition: A one-to-one matching between two sets where every element in one set is paired with exactly one element in the other, and vice versa.
definitions.example: Like pairing each student in a class with a unique desk—no empty desks and no students standing.

definitions.definition: A mathematical object that describes relationships between vectors and scalars, often used in physics for forces and fields.
definitions.example: Like a spreadsheet that holds numbers describing how things stretch or twist in different directions.

definitions.definition: The study of what exists—what kinds of things are real.
definitions.example: Like asking 'Is a thought real in the same way a rock is real?'

definitions.definition: The study of knowledge—how we know what we know.
definitions.example: Like asking 'How do you know that the sun will rise tomorrow?'

definitions.definition: Something that depends on something else for its existence; not necessary.
definitions.example: Like an ice cube that depends on the freezer—it wouldn't exist without it.

definitions.definition: Something that must exist and cannot not exist; it depends on nothing else.
definitions.example: Like the number 2—it has to exist for math to work.

definitions.definition: A theoretical field in the Theophysics framework that represents God's grace or invitation, with a nonzero ground state.
definitions.example: Like an invisible signal that is always broadcasting, even when no one is listening.
definitions.first_appearance: V The Father and the Floor

definitions.definition: A mathematical function that measures how 'in sync' or aligned a system is with God's order.
definitions.example: Like a score that tells you how well a choir is singing together.

definitions.definition: A concept describing how sin or moral failure bends or distorts the spiritual 'space' around a person.
definitions.example: Like a heavy ball on a rubber sheet that creates a dip—sin creates a 'dip' in moral reality.

definitions.definition: Based on observation or experiment, not just theory.
definitions.example: Like testing a recipe by actually baking the cake and tasting it.

definitions.definition: Able to be proven wrong by evidence or experiment.
definitions.example: Like the claim 'all swans are white'—it can be proven false by finding one black swan.

definitions.definition: A basic statement that is accepted as true without proof, used as a starting point for reasoning.
definitions.example: Like 'a straight line is the shortest distance between two points' in geometry.

definitions.definition: A statement that has been proven to be true using logic and axioms.
definitions.example: Like the Pythagorean theorem: a² + b² = c² for right triangles.

definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; the tendency for things to become more mixed up over time.
definitions.example: Like a tidy room that naturally gets messy if you don't clean it.
definitions.first_appearance: V The Father and the Floor

definitions.definition: The process by which a quantum system loses its quantum properties and behaves like a classical system, often due to interaction with the environment.
definitions.example: Like a spinning top that slowly wobbles and stops due to friction with the air.
definitions.first_appearance: V The Father and the Floor

definitions.definition: A mathematical function that summarizes the dynamics of a system, used to derive equations of motion.
definitions.example: Like a recipe that tells you how a system will evolve over time.

definitions.definition: A natural vibration pattern of a system, where all parts oscillate at the same frequency.
definitions.example: Like the specific way a guitar string vibrates when you pluck it to produce a certain note.

definitions.definition: A field that gives particles mass by interacting with them; it has a nonzero value even in empty space.
definitions.example: Like a thick syrup that slows down particles moving through it, giving them 'weight.'
definitions.first_appearance: V The Father and the Floor

definitions.definition: The average value of a field in the vacuum state; for the Higgs field, it is nonzero, meaning the vacuum has a constant background value.
definitions.example: Like the background hum of a refrigerator that is always there, even when nothing else is happening.
definitions.first_appearance: V The Father and the Floor

definitions.definition: A term used to describe the Son's eternal relationship with the Father, meaning the Son comes from the Father in a unique way, not created but 'born' of the Father.
definitions.example: Like a beam of light coming from a flashlight—the beam is not separate from the flashlight but comes from it.
definitions.first_appearance: IV Why the Hiddenness Is Not a Bug

definitions.definition: A term used to describe the Holy Spirit's relationship to the Father (and sometimes the Son), meaning the Spirit comes from the Father.
definitions.example: Like a river flowing from a spring—the water comes from the source.
definitions.first_appearance: IV Why the Hiddenness Is Not a Bug

definitions.definition: The process of obtaining something from a source or origin.
definitions.example: Like getting flour from wheat by grinding it.
definitions.first_appearance: IV Why the Hiddenness Is Not a Bug

definitions.definition: Cannot be made smaller or simpler; the smallest possible amount.
definitions.example: Like the smallest LEGO brick that can't be broken into smaller pieces.

definitions.definition: Removed or emptied out completely.
definitions.example: Like sucking all the air out of a bottle to create a vacuum.

definitions.definition: Spreads throughout every part of something.
definitions.example: Like water soaking into a sponge until it's wet all the way through.

definitions.definition: Something that must be true because of the way a system is built or organized.
definitions.example: Like a door needing a hinge to swing open—it's not optional, it's built into the design.

definitions.definition: A rule that describes what happens at the edges of a system, like the fixed ends of a guitar string.
definitions.example: Like the walls of a swimming pool that determine how waves bounce back.

definitions.definition: A part of an equation that describes how something changes over time or in response to forces.
definitions.example: Like the part of a car's engine that makes it move, not just sit still.

definitions.definition: A set of four equations that describe how electricity and magnetism work and how they are related.
definitions.example: Like the rules that explain how a magnet picks up a paperclip or how a light bulb glows.

definitions.definition: The process where an atom or molecule in an excited state releases energy as light without any external trigger.
definitions.example: Like a glow-in-the-dark sticker that shines after being in the light, without you doing anything to it.

definitions.definition: A detailed plan or design that shows how something is built, used metaphorically for God's plan for creation.
definitions.example: Like the drawings an architect makes before building a house.

definitions.definition: Something that stands between two things and helps them connect or communicate.
definitions.example: Like a translator who helps two people who speak different languages understand each other.

definitions.definition: The idea that the Son (Logos) is the timeless logic or plan of God.
definitions.example: Like the unchanging rules of math that have always been true.

definitions.definition: Something that does not change, even when other things do.
definitions.example: Like the total amount of money in a closed jar, no matter how you move coins around.
